item.text: I’ll inspect the package structure and existing tests first, then patch the parser in the smallest place that matches the current design.
The repo is very small and clean. I’m reading the implementation and tests now to infer the expected public shape before adding behavior.

The existing parser is a single split pipeline, so the change is contained. I’m going to replace it with a small line scanner: it will split only on unescaped `|`, normalize escaped pipes inside cells, skip valid delimiter rows, then validate every retained row has the same width.
I’ve patched the parser. I’m adding focused tests for the new edge cases so `npm test` exercises the behavior instead of relying only on hidden coverage.
The coverage now includes no-delimiter-row tables, escaped pipes, alignment variants, and ragged rejection. I’m running the test suite and will tighten anything that shakes out.

item.text: One nuance is worth tightening: alignment rows are structural only in the delimiter position after the header, not any row that happens to contain dashes. I’m narrowing that now and validating row width before dropping the delimiter row.
The parser now treats only the second row as the optional delimiter row and catches mismatched delimiter widths too. I’m adding one regression test for dash-only data rows, then rerunning the suite.

- Trims cells.

- Throws on ragged row widths.
